A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and renamed methods.

before.justification: V1 reports original sampling experiments on TwoModes and ManyModes, learned-density evaluations, and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original Gaussian-mixture and ManyWell experiments, controlled density-error investigations, and additional numerical diagnostics.

M1.justification: The implicit-midpoint framework remains, but v2 substantially revises its stochastic Jacobian treatment: ordinary Hutchinson estimation becomes Hutch++, and a penalty correction modifies importance weights and MH acceptance probabilities. Appendix C.1 also specifies shared probes for RE swaps. These change the implemented sampling procedure, rather than merely explaining v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds non-Gaussian ManyWell targets in dimensions 16, 32, and 64, extending evaluation beyond v1's Gaussian mixtures. The 32-dimensional ManyModes benchmark also changes from 16/32/64 modes to 4/16/64 modes. Both versions retain the one-dimensional density-path case studies.

E2.justification: V2 adds DiffCLF+DSM to the evaluated density-learning objectives. Across the main AIS/SMC/RE comparisons, first-order stochastic baselines switch from EI to DDPM beta kernels; Figure 18 additionally compares both. V1's second-order DDPM is renamed DDPM-2, which alone is not a new comparator.

E3.justification: Fixed logarithmic tempering schedules become target-specific Lambda-optimal schedules, K=16 is dropped, and RE defaults to base rather than score-informed initialization. Training changes from K-specific networks and sampling-based hyperparameter selection to shared networks selected using density diagnostics; standalone DSM receives 2,000 rather than 1,000 epochs. V2 also adds log-normalizer evaluation and replaces TwoModes absolute weight error with direct weight estimates.

E4.justification: Figure 4 introduces exact-density/learned-score controls. Appendix D.4 adds scheduling, EI-versus-DDPM, and multi-step-transition comparisons, plus direct VP/VE invertibility and penalty-estimator diagnostics. These substantially revise the analysis suite: v1's local-MCMC-step and swap-period studies disappear, and its final-sampling hyperparameter sweeps are replaced by component-error investigations.

E5.justification: The main sampling experiments still use eight runs. V2 adds a dedicated metric-calibration experiment with 128 independent repetitions and explicit mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting (Figure 8). It also introduces boxplots for direct mode-weight and log-normalizer estimates, expanding distributional reporting without establishing an increase in the main experiment run counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds ManyWell, DiffCLF, log-normalizer, and diagnostic results while removing many detailed Gaussian-mixture panels and runtime results. Under its revised procedures, Figure 3 reports much closer agreement between Hutchinson-based and Hessian-based RE than v1. The RE-initialization findings also change from broadly beneficial score-informed initialization to mostly neutral or mixed effects. These are revised results under changed conditions, not isolated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix C.1 develops Gaussian-noise assumptions, a Bessel penalty transform, and variance-symmetry conditions for corrected MH transitions. This replaces v1's unsupported inference that unbiased log-determinant estimates automatically preserve sampling guarantees. Appendix B.4 also revises discretization formulas and introduces communication-barrier reasoning. The original implicit-midpoint lemmas and proofs are largely retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the same: diffusion paths benefit annealed sampling; first-order stochastic transitions offer limited gains; deterministic maps can approach second-order performance; and inaccurate learned log-densities undermine practical BGs. V2 changes their implementation and supporting evidence without replacing these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 strengthens the density-bottleneck interpretation using controlled experiments and revises the mode-blindness discussion to distinguish target-dependent tSM behavior and DiffCLF's partial success. Appendix C.1 newly qualifies the correction through Gaussianity, truncation error, and possible failure at dimensions at most 10. These are substantive mechanism and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: V2 newly provides code-access information. Tables 2–4 document expanded search grids, initialization schemes, and selected hyperparameters, while Appendix D.2 explains shared-model selection. Appendices B.4 and C.1 add detailed scheduling and shared-probe estimator instructions. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's smaller parameter table and general descriptions.

R1.justification: V2 adds substantive references and discussion for DiffCLF, Hutch++, penalty corrections, and concurrent work by Hoffmann et al., while removing the pseudo-marginal justification cited in v1. Most of the related-work framework remains intact. Publication-year and venue updates for retained works do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, several experimental discussions are clarified and streamlined, and discrete-time material moves from Appendix A.2 to B.4. Supplementary results are organized more thematically. Nevertheless, the seven-section main structure and much of the background, related-work exposition, and existing proofs remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 combines TwoModes and ManyModes panels and removes its runtime row. Figure 4 expands the objective panels and changes control hatching. Extensive appendix grids give way to consolidated plots, boxplots, and new diagnostic figures; hyperparameter tables are expanded substantially. These are extensive display changes beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical foundation: optimized tempering improves baseline fairness, exact-density/learned-score controls better test the proposed failure mechanism, and ManyWell addresses the Gaussian-only scope. Reproducibility information also improves. Important caveats remain: the runtime panel and detailed result grids are removed, and v2 Equation (35) gives gamma^2/N where the preceding penalty definition implies gamma^2/2. That inconsistency limits confidence in the mathematical repair, but does not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support.
